package_info.package_name: typosquatted variants of popular NPM packages (e.g., shebang-command, ignore, webidl-conversions, debug, supports-colors, anymatch, universalify, http-errors, micromatch, postcss-value-parse, glob-parent, string-width, ansi-regex, tslib, y18n)
package_info.package_versions: all published versions during the attack window (Oct 2, 2022, 12:00 AM UTC - 6:00 PM UTC)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are typosquatted clones of popular NPM packages, designed to deceive developers into installing them. Upon installation, they execute a malicious preinstall script that downloads and runs a Windows shortcut (.lnk) file, which in turn executes a PowerShell script to bypass UAC and exfiltrate user credentials. This behavior is entirely unrelated to the expected functionality of the legitimate packages and constitutes a severe supply chain attack targeting developer environments.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (preinstall), the package.json preinstall hook triggers execution of index.js, enabling arbitrary code execution before the package is fully installed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of a preinstall hook to execute a custom script is highly unusual for utility libraries and can enable arbitrary code execution on the installer's system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely use preinstall hooks, and when they do, it is typically for environment checks or build steps, not for executing arbitrary scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages use preinstall for build preparation or environment validation, but not for downloading and executing remote files or binaries.
key_indicators: Presence of preinstall hook in package.json
Execution of local JavaScript file (index.js) during install
Ability to run arbitrary code at install time

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (preinstall), index.js downloads a Windows shortcut (.lnk) file from a remote server to the package directory and executes it, resulting in further code execution on the victim's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing a remote .lnk file during installation is a clear indicator of malicious intent, as it allows the attacker to run arbitrary code on the installer's system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not download and execute remote binaries or shortcut files as part of their installation process, especially not without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download platform-specific binaries, but never via .lnk files or without explicit user approval.
key_indicators: Download of .lnk (Windows shortcut) file from hardcoded remote URL
Execution of downloaded file via child_process.exec
Network request to external domain during install

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution (child process from index.js), the .lnk file launches PowerShell via cmd.exe to download a VBS script from a remote server, saves it to the temp directory, executes the VBS script to bypass UAC and exfiltrate credentials, and opens Notepad as a decoy.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Chaining cmd.exe, PowerShell, and VBS to download and execute remote scripts is a classic malware technique. The use of UAC bypass and credential exfiltration is overtly malicious and not found in legitimate packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should ever execute such a chain of commands, especially not for a utility library. Executing remote scripts and attempting UAC bypass is strictly malicious.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There are no legitimate use cases for this behavior in NPM packages.
key_indicators: Use of PowerShell to download and execute remote VBS script
Opening Notepad as a decoy process

attack_chain.action: During installation, the preinstall hook in package.json triggers execution of index.js.
index.js downloads a malicious Windows shortcut (.lnk) file from a remote server and saves it locally, then executes the .lnk file.
The .lnk file executes a command that launches PowerShell to download and run a VBS script, which performs UAC bypass and exfiltrates credentials.

behavioral_signatures: NPM package with preinstall hook executing custom JavaScript file (index.js)
Installation-time download and execution of .lnk (Windows shortcut) files
Child process execution of PowerShell or VBS scripts from NPM install context
Network requests to known malicious domains during package installation
file_indicators: index.js containing code to download and execute remote files
Temporary VBS scripts (e.g., p.vbs) in %tmp% directory
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for NPM packages that define a preinstall hook in package.json, especially those that execute scripts downloading and running remote files. Flag any installation process that downloads .lnk files or invokes PowerShell/VBS scripts. Alert on network connections to known malicious domains or IPs during package installation. Review for unexpected files (e.g., README.txt.lnk) in package directories and temporary VBS scripts (e.g., p.vbs) in user temp folders. Correlate these behaviors to identify supply chain attacks.
